concept.technique_name: blank-by-blank clue matching in a three-blank text completion

examples.problem_statement: The fact that the average life expectancy ten thousand years ago was so much shorter than it is now is often (i) ________ as evidence supporting the notion that the world always improves with time. However, if you (ii) _________ for the fact that most children in that epoch died in childbirth, it turns out that life expectancy back then was nearly the same as it is now. On a (iii) _________ note, it also turns out that many “barbaric” hunter-gatherer tribes were taller on average than the average person now living.

solution.operation: Blank (i): read the clause "shorter life expectancy ten thousand years ago ... as evidence supporting the notion that the world always improves with time"
solution.description: Begin with blank (i), where a fact about life expectancy is being related to the claim that the world improves with time; because longer life expectancy today would genuinely support that claim, the fact is simply being put forward as evidence, so the plain reporting word cited fills the blank.

solution.operation: Blank (ii): apply the signal "However ... if you _____ for the fact that most children in that epoch died in childbirth"
solution.description: Handle blank (ii) by noticing that the sentence says the statistic is misleading once a new fact is taken into account; the blank therefore needs a verb meaning to adjust the figure for that new piece of information, which gives correct (correct for).

solution.operation: Blank (iii): compare the final sentence's topic (average height of hunter-gatherer tribes) with the preceding topic (life expectancy)
solution.description: For blank (iii), observe that the last sentence suddenly shifts from life expectancy to height, so the note is slightly off the main topic; choose tangential to mark that shift.

solution.operation: Check the blank (iii) distractor "sidereal" against its actual definition
solution.result: sidereal rejected: it means "related to the stars"
solution.description: Before committing to blank (iii), test the tempting look-alike sidereal: despite resembling "side," it has nothing to do with being off to the side and instead means related to the stars, so it cannot describe an off-topic remark.

key_reminders: Fill the blank whose clue is most explicit first; here blank (i) is anchored by the "evidence supporting" phrase.
A contrast signal such as "However" tells you the second blank must adjust or qualify the earlier statistic, not repeat it.
Match a word to its real definition, not to a familiar-looking root inside it.
common_mistakes: Choosing disregarded for blank (i), which reverses the logic — the fact is being used as evidence, not dismissed.
Picking sidereal for blank (iii) because it looks like "side," when it actually means related to the stars.
Reading the height sentence as contradicting the life-expectancy discussion rather than as a side note, and so wanting a contrast word instead of tangential.
